description: Committee recommends early procurement for 2027-2028 road, sidewalk projects.
This two-year pilot covers up to 60% of program funding.
Aims to improve project delivery and competitive bidding.

chips.text: Recommended
Councillor Ford and Mayor Block praised the proposal as forward-thinking.
Taxpayers could save money through improved competitive bidding.
Construction Association of Saskatchewan wholeheartedly supports early procurement.
Administration recommends a two-year pilot to evaluate results and industry feedback.

description: Adds transit signal images and operating rules to bylaw.
Authorizes specific vehicles in dedicated transit lanes.
Prohibits unauthorized vehicles from transit lanes.
Amends Saskatoon Transit bus stop definitions.

chips.text: Recommended
Councillor raised concerns about SGI approval and potential legal jeopardy.
Drivers and visitors will be affected by new transit rules.
Question about SGI approval and potential legal jeopardy remained unanswered publicly.
Potential legal risks flagged regarding provincial Traffic Safety Act amendments.

description: City monitors winter road maintenance contractor performance.
Poor contractor performance can lead to contract termination.
Contractors can be barred from future city bids.

chips.text: Councillor Donauer emphasized focusing on best value, not just lowest price.
Residents in neighborhoods outside Circle Drive are affected by contractor performance.
Administration does not recommend rotating contractors between service areas.
City terminated a contract and barred a poor-performing contractor from future bids.
Using past performance in bids requires careful, defensible procurement practices.
Staff committed to continuously refining and improving winter road maintenance processes.

description: City will not coordinate priority street snow grading with waste collection.
Will track complaints and document local street snow grading practices.

chips.text: Limited direct impact on residents from current priority street snow grading.
Resident surveys show high satisfaction with waste collection, no snow grading concerns.

description: City continues discussions on upfront taxi fares for driver safety.
Research compares operating expenses for small and large taxis.
Report on taxi fare changes expected Q4 2026 to Q1 2027.

chips.text: Taxi drivers are greatly impacted by potential upfront fare changes.
Taxi drivers' union welcomes safety discussions, but opposes mandatory safety shields due to cost.

speakers.name: Malik Draz
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Taxi Items
said: Union welcomes driver safety discussions; encourages voluntary safety shield installation.
Does not recommend mandatory safety shields due to significant cost.
Appreciates initial report's decision to collect fares upfront.

description: Sets a $9.50 large vehicle taxi fare.
Requires taxi brokerages to supply driver equipment.
Limits large vehicle fare to passenger-requested trips.

chips.text: Administration explained the $9.50 fare flattens costs to cover vehicle capital.
Taxi drivers face reduced income from the new large vehicle rates.
A survey showed 63% of stakeholders opposed new large vehicle rates.
Administration will work with the driver with a debit machine lease until October 2027.

description: Improves snow clearing near 60 senior complexes for accessibility.
City explores three options for enhanced snow removal services.
Administration will develop cost estimates for these options.

chips.text: Councillor questioned why resident service request data was excluded from the report.
Administration will continue refining snow removal practices at problem locations.

description: Strong Towns YXE raised concerns about unsafe pedestrian crossing times.
City crosswalks may not meet current national safety standards.
Administration estimates five more years to update all signals.

chips.text: Recommended
Administration explained signal updates are complex, not just 'clicking a couple buttons'.
Staff prioritized major road planning over accelerating crosswalk updates for new resources.
Administration has not compared Saskatoon's signal update pace to other cities.
Over 85 residents reported feeling rushed or unsafe crossing city intersections.
Short crossing times disproportionately affect seniors, children

speakers.name: Zachary De Francesco
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Addressing Substandard Signalized Crosswalk Times
said: Many signalized crosswalks have substandard crossing times, making them unsafe.
A case study showed a 30-meter crosswalk provides 26 seconds, but TAC requires 30.
City should create a plan to audit and update all intersections to meet TAC standards.

description: City can boot vehicles on private property for unpaid parking tickets.
Saskatoon has $6.6 million in outstanding parking ticket debt.

chips.text: Recommended
Saskatoon taxpayers are affected by $6.6 million in uncollected debt.
Administration will report on parking ticket collection strategy in Q4 this year.
